rascunho-em-bloco.d: Speculation strategy in which the drafter proposes every position of the block in a single parallel forward, instead of one token per forward (like MTP and EAGLE). Examples: DFlash/DFlash2 and DSpark.

token-ancora.d: First token of the draft block: the last verified token (the bonus emitted by the target). The remaining positions of the block are masks or noise.

difusao-em-bloco.d: Family of models that fill a block of masked positions in parallel, with bidirectional attention inside the block. DFlash uses this idea as a drafter: [anchor, MASK×7] → 7 tokens in one forward.

token-mascara.d: Special id that occupies the not-yet-written positions of the draft block. GLM/DFlash2: 154856 (in the vocabulary's padding range); DeepSeek/DSpark: dspark_noise_token_id 128799.

injecao-de-kv.d: In DFlash/DSpark, the target's hidden states at already-verified positions are projected into keys and values for each drafter layer; the queries come only from the block. The drafter never has to reprocess the prompt.

suffix-decay.d: Drop in draft quality at the final positions of a block predicted in parallel. E.g. GLM on prose: acceptance 0.75 at position 1 and 0.06 at position 7.

conv-dinamica.d: In DFlash2: each block position is mixed with the previous one (2 taps), with coefficients = learned base + a correction generated by the token itself, shared across groups of 16 channels. It never crosses the block boundary.

seletor-de-candidatos.d: DFlash2 component that keeps the top-16 candidates at each position and scores transitions between neighboring positions with rank-256 bilinear codebooks; a walk (argmax or Gumbel-max) picks a coherent path.

colisao-multimodal.d: When positions are predicted in parallel, each follows its marginal distribution; if there are two plausible continuations, the per-position argmax can blend them (“New Lake City”).

markov-head.d: Logit bias W2·W1[previous token], a low-rank (256) bigram applied left to right on top of the logits of DSpark's parallel backbone. Each matrix is 129,280 × 256 (≈66 MB in BF16).

confidence-head.d: Linear(hidden + 256 → 1) with a sigmoid that estimates the probability of each draft being accepted; trained against 1 − TV(p, q). It feeds the confidence-based verification schedulers.

sobrevivencia-prefixo.d: Probability that the first j drafts are all accepted: the product of the conditional acceptances, a_j = Π c_i. Summing the a_j gives the expected tokens per step.

adaptive-k.d: Verifying only a prefix of the proposed drafts, with the length chosen from recent statistics (EMA on GLM) or from predicted confidence (DSpark). It is lossless because the length is chosen before verifying the current step, using only past (EMA) or predicted (confidence) information; the rejection sampling of each verified position remains exact.

ema.d: e ← α·obs + (1 − α)·e. Summarizes the recent past with weights that decay geometrically; a larger α reacts faster and oscillates more.

condensacao-do-lote.d: In vLLM V1 continuous batching, when a request finishes, other requests are moved to fill the empty batch row. Auxiliary state indexed by row, rather than by request, ends up belonging to the wrong request.

lote-ragged.d: Flattened batch in which each request contributes a different number of rows (e.g. a prefill chunk + decodes). The boundaries are given by query_start_loc, the cumulative offsets of each segment.

regra-de-parada.d: Rule that decides, each round, where to cut the draft chain. In TensorFold: fN (always N), fcN:P (up to N while the product of the noise-free confidences is ≥ P), fncN:P (the same product with confidences aware of the keyed noise) and fcostN (the k that maximizes expected tokens per millisecond). With equality verification, the rule changes only the speed, never the reply.

log-loss.d: A calibration measure of predicted probabilities against 0/1 outcomes: \( -\frac{1}{n}\sum [y\log q + (1-y)\log(1-q)] \). It punishes confident wrong predictions. TensorFold used it to fit the \(\beta = 2.0\) of the noise-aware confidences.

replay-de-politicas.d: Evaluating draft rules on the CPU from a teacher-forced dump. With keyed sampling, the committed tokens don't depend on the rule, so each round of any rule keeps exactly the drafts equal to those tokens, and a cost table turns the rounds into tok/s (the simulator of TensorFold's patch 0011).

oraculo-de-profundidade.d: A dynamic program with hindsight that picks, for each round, the number of drafts that minimizes total time, knowing in advance how many would match. No real rule reaches it; it serves as a ceiling for stop rules (oracle7 in TensorFold's simulator).

linhas-lixo.d: Rows reserved at the end of a pool where the padding rows of a launch captured as a CUDA graph write. In TensorFold's multi-conversation drafter, capture and warmup use tables that send everything to the trash, so they never touch a live conversation's state.
